audit.title: CCIP Directory - Mainnet

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Weak. The page opens `# CCIP Directory` → `## Networks mainnet (78)` with no self-contained sentence a model can lift to answer "what networks/tokens does CCIP support on mainnet?" The headline count (78) is buried in a heading, not a claim.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Reasonable — 41 headings, 1 H1, max depth H3, 0 level skips (measured). But sections are tiny (median 4 words), there are 0 tables and 0 bullets, and the data lives in link cards rather than an extractable table.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Good for a directory — per-chain specifics like "Ethereum 77 lanes | 206 tokens," plus totals (78 networks, 275 tokens); 38 numerals measured. Missing: chain IDs, no units on counts, and no aggregate breakdown in liftable prose.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 40 links, all internal, 0 external/primary (measured). No link to the CCIP concepts/architecture page or a definition of "lane" from this hub.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Very weak. No one-sentence definition of CCIP, "lane," or "token pool" anywhere on the page. Nothing verbatim-liftable defines the entity.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Two valid JSON-LD blocks (`DataCatalog` + `BreadcrumbList`), canonical URL, 12 og + 9 twitter tags, `article:modified_time` 2025-05-19, and JSON-LD `dateModified` 2026-09-21 with `inLanguage` en-US. The `DataCatalog` lists all 78 chains as `Dataset` nodes with URLs — highly agent-parseable. Note: the measured-facts "datePublished/dateModified absent" refers to the absence of an Article/TechArticle date; freshness signals do exist in `<head>` and the DataCatalog.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Not applicable — a directory needs no snippets; not penalized.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Devs/agents ask "does CCIP support Solana?", "what tokens can I bridge with CCIP?", "how many chains does CCIP support?" No heading is phrased as any of these, and the "See more" collapse hides most of the answer from text extraction.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; naming is consistent (chain names, token symbols) and unambiguous. Only limitation is sparseness, not confusion.

audit.summary: This is a CCIP mainnet directory/index page: a listing of 78 supported networks (with per-chain lane and token counts) and 275 tokens, backed by an excellent `DataCatalog` JSON-LD block that enumerates all 78 chains with canonical URLs. Its biggest GEO strength is machine-readable structured data; its biggest weakness is the near-total absence of framing prose — no answer-first sentence, no definition of CCIP or "lane," and most of the listing hidden behind "See more" so the rendered text exposes only 14 of 78 chains and 24 of 275 tokens. The honest verdict: a strong data substrate wrapped in prose too thin to win the "does CCIP support X?" and "what chains/tokens does CCIP support?" queries this page should own.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first intro paragraph with headline stats
recommendations.mapsTo: answer-first extractability, quotable definitions, concrete specifics
recommendations.where: directly under `# CCIP Directory`, before `## Networks mainnet (78)`
recommendations.issue: page jumps straight to a listing; no liftable summary sentence.
recommendations.change: add 2–3 sentences, e.g. "The Chainlink CCIP mainnet directory lists every blockchain and token supported by the Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol in production. As of the last update, CCIP supports 78 mainnet networks and 275 tokens. Each network page lists its active lanes (source→destination routes) and supported tokens."
recommendations.why: gives engines a self-contained, quotable answer to "what/how many does CCIP support" — the dominant query this page should win.

recommendations.title: Expose the full network and token lists (don't gate behind "See more")
recommendations.issue: rendered content shows only 14/78 chains and 24/275 tokens; the rest is client-side hidden.
recommendations.change: render the complete lists in server HTML (progressive disclosure via CSS, not omission), so a skim or RAG chunk can confirm "is Zircuit / is GHO supported?"
recommendations.why: retrieval and extraction fail on entities absent from served text; a page that omits 82% of tokens can't answer most support-check queries.

recommendations.title: Add token enumeration to structured data
recommendations.issue: `DataCatalog` enumerates all 78 chains but no tokens; the 275 tokens exist only as (mostly hidden) link cards.
recommendations.change: add the token list as `Dataset`/`DefinedTermSet` entries (name + URL) mirroring the chain datasets.
recommendations.why: makes token-support facts API-able for agents even when body text is collapsed.

recommendations.title: Add a summary comparison table of networks
recommendations.issue: 0 tables; lane/token counts sit in link cards that don't extract cleanly.
recommendations.change: a `Network | Lanes | Tokens | Chain page` table for all 78 rows.
recommendations.why: tables are high-lift for engines extracting comparative/quantitative answers ("which chain has the most lanes?").

recommendations.title: Define "lane" and "token pool" inline
recommendations.where: in the new intro or a one-line note above the network list
recommendations.issue: "77 lanes | 206 tokens" appears with no definition of "lane."
recommendations.change: "A lane is a directional route between a source and destination chain," linked to the CCIP architecture/concepts page.
recommendations.why: supplies a crisp liftable definition and an authoritative internal citation, both currently absent.

recommendations.title: Add question-phrased subheadings
recommendations.issue: headings are entity labels ("Networks mainnet (78)"), not questions users type.
recommendations.change: add/rename to "Which networks does CCIP support on mainnet?" and "Which tokens does CCIP support on mainnet?"
recommendations.why: symptom/question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Surface a visible last-updated line
recommendations.issue: freshness lives only in metadata (`dateModified` 2026-09-21); no on-page signal.
recommendations.why: visible freshness raises trust/E-E-A-T for a fast-changing directory.

antiPatterns: **Content hidden from extraction:** "See more" collapses omit 82% of tokens and 82% of chains from served text — the single largest retrieval risk here.
**Wall-free but definition-free:** no undefined-jargon walls, but key terms ("lane") are used without any definition.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references — clean on those.
offPageNotes: Consider an `llms.txt` entry pointing agents at the CCIP directory as the canonical source for supported-network/token facts.

The `DataCatalog` schema is a genuine asset — ensure the sibling `directory/testnet` and per-chain pages cross-link back to this hub to reinforce it as the canonical directory (canonical-hub pattern).
Site-level: the measured "datePublished/dateModified absent" applies to the Article-type date; adding those to a `TechArticle`/`Dataset` wrapper would remove the ambiguity across tooling.
